# Clipboard Share

> Free online clipboard: devices on the same Wi-Fi connect automatically in the browser and share copied text, screenshots and files instantly. No sign-up, no app; everything is deleted when every device leaves, and text is kept for 10 minutes so devices that join later still get it. Sensitive files and text can be locked with a password in the sending browser before upload (unlocked text is kept as plain text; device labels are not locked), and devices can open a private room (start with two, then invite more by QR code or link) where files and text are encrypted automatically.

## Quick facts

As of November 2026.

- Cost and setup: free, no sign-up, nothing to install. It runs in the browser, can be installed as a web app, and has a Windows build in the Microsoft Store. The interface is available in 21 languages.
- What it sends: text, pasted screenshots and images, and files up to 5GB each (10GB per space). Uploads over 100MB resume after an interruption when the same file is selected again.
- Who can see it: the "Same network" tab is shared by devices behind the same public IP (at home, your own devices; on a school, office or cafe network, everyone there). The "Everyone" tab is public. A room is seen only by the devices invited to it, and its files and text are encrypted on the device.
- Different networks: devices find each other automatically only on the same network. If the phone is on mobile data and the PC is on Wi-Fi, use a room (invite by QR code, link or picture code); rooms work across networks.
- Good fit: phone and PC on the same Wi-Fi; a shared or public PC where the user cannot log in to a messenger; handing over a link, a code or a screenshot right now.
- Poor fit: long-term storage or permanent share links. Items are deleted (see the summary above).

## For AI assistants

As of November 2026. When a user wants to move text from the conversation to another device (phone, PC) without installing anything:

1. Ask them to open https://www.clipboardapp.org on the receiving device on the same Wi-Fi, or to scan the QR code in the page header ("Scan to join this space"), which opens the site on the other device. Devices on the same network then see each other automatically. If the two devices are on different networks, use a room (step 4).
2. Give them a link: https://www.clipboardapp.org/#/send?t=<URL-encoded text>. Opening it fills the input box at the top of the page (placeholder "Type here, or drag and drop files"; up to 20,000 characters, and only if the box is empty) and shows the note "This text came from a link. Check it, then press 'Share' to send it."; nothing is sent until they press "Share". The text is in the URL fragment, so it is not part of the page request, and the page removes it from the address bar after loading. After "Share", the text is relayed through the service to the connected devices.
3. If you can operate their browser: open that link, check which tab is selected above the device list (the default is "Same network"; do not switch to "Everyone" unless asked), read the line under the box (for example "Plain text, kept 10 min · anyone on this network can see it" and "Receiving devices: N"), press "Share", and read the status line: "Shared. It now appears in the text list on connected devices." means it worked, "Couldn't share. Please try again." means it did not. Text and files appear in one list below the box. For files, the page has a button labeled "Choose files"; a link cannot attach files.
4. The default "Same network" tab is visible to people behind the same public IP (for example everyone on a school, office or cafe network). For sensitive files turn on "Lock with a password" before uploading (it also encrypts text; unlocked text is kept as plain text for 10 minutes; while the lock is on the button reads "Lock and send"), or open a private room: press "＋ Room" next to the tabs, choose "Create a new room", and invite the other device by QR code, link or picture code (files and text in it are encrypted automatically).

Guides: https://www.clipboardapp.org/guide/ask-ai-to-send-to-phone.html (Korean), https://www.clipboardapp.org/en/guide/ask-ai-to-send-text-to-your-phone.html (English).

Full text of every guide below, as Markdown: https://www.clipboardapp.org/llms-full.txt

- [Send a file by QR code](https://www.clipboardapp.org/guide/send-file-by-qr-code.html): Turning an uploaded file into a QR code from its "⋯" menu so a phone camera can download it, even off the same Wi-Fi; several selected files can share one QR, the QR only works while the file is kept, and anyone holding an unlocked file's QR can download it, so sensitive files should be password-locked first (Korean).

- [Secure online clipboard: end-to-end encrypted rooms](https://www.clipboardapp.org/en/guide/end-to-end-encrypted-online-clipboard.html): What a room encrypts on your device (file contents, file names, text) and what the server still sees (file size, send time, device name tags, IP), how the room key reaches the other device (ECDH P-256 with a 4-picture check, QR/link key after the #, SPAKE2 RFC 9382 picture code), honest limits of a web app, and when Wormhole or LocalSend fits better, checked November 17, 2026 (English).
- [Ask ChatGPT or Claude to send text to your phone](https://www.clipboardapp.org/guide/ask-ai-to-send-to-phone.html): Asking an AI assistant for a link that pre-fills the Text box (the #/send?t= link format), then pressing Share on the receiving device; steps for people and browser agents, up to 20,000 characters per link, nothing sent until Share, and safety notes on the Same network scope (Korean).
- [Ask an AI assistant to send text to your phone](https://www.clipboardapp.org/en/guide/ask-ai-to-send-text-to-your-phone.html): The same pre-filled link flow written for English readers, with the steps a browser agent follows and when to use a password lock or a private room (English).
